summary: On 29 May 2026, OpenAI reported degraded access across 12 ChatGPT components: Conversations, Login, Compliance API, Search, File uploads, Voice mode, GPTs, Image Generation, Deep Research, Agent, ChatGPT Atlas and Connectors/Apps. OpenAI began investigating at 13:20 and declared all impacted services fully recovered at 13:28, an eight-minute public incident window. The provider did not disclose a technical root cause, affected-user count or regional distribution. The event began more than eight hours after an earlier login and account-creation incident had been resolved.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Complete review of VIGIL Failure Taxonomy 0.6.6 retains the occurrence as unclassified because the first-party evidence establishes a brief, broad ChatGPT access incident but not a reusable failure mechanism. VIGIL-FC-000032 Access-State Differentiation is rejected because listing multiple degraded components does not show two or more materially distinct access causes, restrictions or recovery paths represented as the same misleading state. VIGIL-FC-000031 Authentication-State Continuity is rejected because no expiry, revocation, refresh, recovery or credential-replacement transition is shown to have propagated incoherently to an active session. VIGIL-FC-000048 Verification-Dependency Access Continuity is rejected because no otherwise valid or unresolved entitlement is shown to have become unavailable solely through a failed dependent verifier without a proportionate fallback. Other selectable classes lack the required occurrence mechanism; temporal proximity to a different incident does not supply one.

classification_review_provenance.authority_boundary: The complete selectable VIGIL Failure Taxonomy 0.6.6 class set was reviewed against the bounded occurrence. Accepted mappings: none. Material rejected candidates: VIGIL-FC-000032 because no collapse of distinct access states is evidenced; VIGIL-FC-000031 because no authentication-state transition propagation defect is evidenced; and VIGIL-FC-000048 because no otherwise valid or unresolved entitlement, failed dependent verifier and absent proportionate fallback are established. The absence of a classification does not deny the outage; it preserves the boundary between observed component degradation and an evidenced governance mechanism.

assessment_boundaries: The public status record establishes affected components and timing but does not disclose a technical root cause, affected-user count or regional distribution.
The published 13:20–13:28 window did not overlap INC-000019's 03:12–04:57 window; same-day occurrence does not establish a shared root cause.
No access-state, authentication-transition or verification-dependency mechanism is inferred from component-level access degradation alone.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: OpenAI's first-party incident page reports access issues across 12 ChatGPT components: Conversations, Login, Compliance API, Search, File uploads, Voice mode, GPTs, Image Generation, Deep Research, Agent, ChatGPT Atlas and Connectors/Apps. The provider began investigating at 13:20 on 2026-05-29 and declared full recovery at 13:28. The public record establishes an eight-minute ChatGPT availability incident but does not identify the technical cause or quantify affected users. Its published window began more than eight hours after the earlier login and account-creation incident was resolved.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The evidenced boundary is broad component availability, not a particular access-authority mechanism. A list of degraded components does not show that distinct access states were conflated, that an authentication transition failed to propagate, or that valid entitlement depended on an unavailable verifier. The provider's investigating and resolved updates preserve the operational sequence, while the absent cause prevents a more specific taxonomy adjudication. Event separation is also substantive: two status incidents on the same date should not be merged when their published windows do not overlap and no common cause is disclosed.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: This incident demonstrates that component breadth and mechanism specificity are different questions. CAM can require clear status scope and event separation while withholding an access-governance classification until causal evidence identifies the actual failed boundary. This avoids turning same-day proximity or a long affected-component list into unsupported mechanism attribution.
